title: HPV test
what: The gynecologist takes a sample from your cervix with a soft brush. The lab checks it for human papillomavirus.
why: To help prevent cervical cancer, usually from age 30; for abnormal Pap test results; before and after cervical treatment.
duration: the sample takes 1 to 2 minutes; results usually come in a few days
tell_doctor: The date of your last period
If you are or might be pregnant
If your cervix was treated recently
If HPV or an abnormal smear was found before

prepare.title: Periods
prepare.text: The sample is not taken during your period. Mid-cycle is best.

prepare.title: 2 days before
prepare.text: No sex, douching, vaginal suppositories, creams, or tampons.

prepare.title: Exam
prepare.text: If a colposcopy is planned, the sample is usually taken before it.

bring: Past smear results, if you have them
steps: You undress below the waist and sit in the exam chair
The doctor inserts a speculum to see the cervix
A soft brush is moved over the cervix for a few seconds
The brush is placed in a tube with liquid
The speculum is removed, and you can get dressed
feel: Pressure and mild discomfort from the speculum
Sometimes a brief cramping pain low in the belly
after: A little spotting the same day is normal
Results usually come in a few days. The lab will tell you when
If HPV is found, your doctor will tell you if you need a Pap test or a colposcopy
red_flags: Heavy bleeding or severe pain low in the belly after the test: see a doctor

faq.a: No. HPV is common and usually goes away by itself. Your doctor keeps watch to catch any changes early.

faq.q: How often should I have an HPV test?
faq.a: Usually every few years if the result is normal. Your doctor will tell you how often.

reminders.text: HPV test in 2 days. Starting today, no sex, suppositories, creams, or douching.
